- Adjust the compensation washers to align the pinion-ring gear when the layshaft has been changed.

1. Move the layshaft (1a) with its new components to the reference surface and measure the height of shaft (1b) from the lower reverse gear washer to the 4th speed surface.

- This measurement is required to align the differential ring gear with the pinion by means of the preload shims located under the differential case bearings.

- Take more than one measurement and calculate the average value.

- Subtract the average height of the new shaft from the average height of the old shaft measured prior to dismantling.

1. If the height difference is negative (new shaft shorter than the old shaft), increase the thickness of compensation washer (1a) and decrease the thickness of compensation washer (1b).

- If the value is positive (new shaft longer than the old shaft), apply the opposite oversized or undersized washers to those described above.

- Remove the differential case bearings

Op. 2110D26 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING BEARINGS - REPLACE WITH DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING REMOVED

- Take the differential case bearing compensation washers.

- Use a micrometer to measure the washer thickness.

- Apply an oversize or undersize to the compensation washers equal to the difference between the measured values (washers vary by 0.05 mm).

- This means that the overall thickness of both compensation washers remains constant because this determines the preload of the differential taper roller bearings.

- During adjustment, the thrust washers must be choosen to achieve the minimum possible tolerance.

- If they do not display evident wear or damage, the washers may be used for the subsequent adjustment operations.

- Refit the differential case bearings
